1. Present appeal is filed under Section 372 Cr.P.C. against the judgment dated 28.03.2023 (hereinafter referred to as impugned order) passed by Ld. Trial Court of Ld.MM (Mahila Court-01),
North whereby the respondent nos.2 to 4 have been acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/ 506/494/107 IPC.
(Parties are hereinafter being referred to by their respective status before the Trial Court).
2. The present criminal appeal has been filed alongwith an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.
It is submitted that the certified copy of the order has been applied on 01.04.2023 and received only on 23/24.04.2023.
Hence, prayer has been made to allow the above said application and condone the delay.
3. The respondents opposed the above said application arguing that the appellant has failed to explain the inordinate delay in filing the present appeal.
4. Arguments heard.
5. Considering the submissions, and the reasons mentioned in the applicant, the delay in filing the present appeal stands condoned and the application is accordingly allowed.

6. Now coming to the appeal on merits, brief facts of the case are that the allegations against accused persons are that complainant Smt. Maya Devi was married with accused Rajan Chawla on 06.07.1995 and during the subsistence of marriage, accused subjected her to cruelty for demand of dowry and compelled her to handover the original documents of her property.

Furthermore, accused misappropriated a part of amount Criminal Appeal No. 182/23 VANDANA Judgment in Maya Devi Vs. Furthermore, accused Renu married co accused Rajan Chawla knowing that such marriage is void by reason of taking place during the life of complainant and thereby committed offence u/s 494 IPC.
7. Accused persons were summoned.
Compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C. was made.
Arguments on order of charge were heard and charge u/s 498-A/406/506/494/496/107 IPC was framed on 21.08.2014 to which they had pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
8. The prosecution had examined total 11 witnesses.

sentences.text: It is well settled that the standard of proof in criminal and civil proceedings are different.
While the prosecution has to prove its case against the accused beyond reasonable doubt in a criminal trial, in the civil proceedings the issue is decided on the preponderance of probabilities.
In my view the judgment passed by a Higher Court exactly on the same issue decided by a civil court, which was upheld by the Hon'ble High Court was binding on the trial court.

sentences.text: 1. Valid First Marriage: The existence of a legally binding first marriage between the accused and their spouse.

2. First Spouse Alive: the first spouse must be alive at the time of the second marriage.
3.Second Marriage Contracted: The accused must have married again.

4. Subsistence of First Marriage : The first marriage must still be legally in effect (not dissolved by divorce, death of annulment).
5. Validity of Second Marriage: The second marriage must also be a valid, complete marriage, meaning all necessary ceremonies

31. The complainant led the entire evidence with respect to the factum of proving her marriage with accused Rajan Chawla and did not lead any single evidence in order to prove the marriage of accused with co accused Renu.
The Proof of the performance of essential ceremonies for the alleged second marriage is inevitably required to prove the offence under section 494 IPC.

In the case in hand, the complainant / appellant neither produced the priest or any other witnesses who had witnessed the alleged second marriage of accused Rajan Chawla with co- accused Renu nor any documentary evidence i.e. any video, photographs, marriage card, marriage certificate, which can establish the factum of alleged marriage of accused Rajan Chawla with co accused Renu.

The complainant only relied upon the testimony of PW-11 Sh. Sheo Dhari Ram who brought the school record of children Deepika, Lakshya Chawla, Sonam and Charu Lata, but he categorically testified that the above documents are of students of Nathu Ram and Pushapa Devi and no record was found with the name of Children of Rajan Chawla and Renu.
The complainant / appellant remained miserably failed to establish the factum of the second marriage as not even a single evidence was led by her in this regard.
She could not bring any single evidence whether oral or documentary to prove that accused persons went through the ceremonies of marriage.
Accordingly, the accused persons were rightly acquitted under section 494/496 IPC.
